hz6_state.topic: Hezbollah in Lebanese politics: elections, 2008 clashes and Doha, the Hariri tribunal, the port blast probe and Tayouneh, the 2019 protests

claims.text: Hezbollah won 8 of 128 seats in 1992 with 4 allied independents in its bloc; 7 in 1996; 10 in 2000; 14 in 2005; 13 in 2009, 2018 and 2022; joined cabinet for first time in 2005 (labour; energy and water), withdrew 2006, rejoined July 2008
2018: Hezbollah and allies won 71 seats; Nasrallah: 'Today I can say that our goals have been achieved'
May 2022: Hezbollah-led coalition won 61 of 128 seats, down about 10, losing its majority; Hezbollah and Amal kept all 27 Shia seats
9 March 2026: parliament voted 76 of 128 to extend its own mandate two years, postponing elections due in May 2026, a week after Hezbollah fired into Israel

The Conversation (Rebeiz) gives 12 seats in 1992 (counting the bloc); Arab Barometer early 2024: 30% of Lebanese trust Hezbollah, 55% not at all; 85% of Shia respondents, 9% Sunni and Druze, 6% Christian

Hezbollah-linked hospitals licensed by Islamic Health Authority; flagship al-Rasool al-Azam; Health Ministry under Diab added 15 Hezbollah-sponsored centres to state-funded list; state funding for Hezbollah-run hospitals rose from about 16bn to 30bn lira
Hamzeh (2004) reports Hezbollah served about 400,000 people with healthcare in 2000; Qassem (2005) says it repaired 17,212 homes damaged by Israeli raids 1991-2000 (Hezbollah's own figure)

6 May 2008 cabinet declared Hezbollah's telephone network illegal and removed Beirut airport security chief; Nasrallah 8 May called it 'a declaration of war'; Hezbollah controlled key areas 9-12 May and handed them to army; govt reversed both decisions 14 May; officials estimated 81 killed, 250+ injured by 12 May
Siniora 10 May 2008 called Hezbollah's actions an attempted coup; Doha agreement 21 May gave opposition 'effective veto'; Suleiman elected 25 May
Hezbollah gunmen knocked Future TV off the air and attacked an affiliated newspaper
2008 deaths: UN June 2008 report 69 killed and 180+ wounded; HRW at least 71; estimates range 70-110; Hezbollah said the network was part of its military apparatus
Doha: 30-minister cabinet 16 majority / 11 opposition / 3 president; parties agreed to ban weapons and violence in political disputes

STL 18 Aug 2020 convicted Salim Ayyash of the 14 Feb 2005 bombing that killed Hariri and 21 others and injured 226; acquitted Merhi, Oneissi, Sabra; no evidence implicating Hezbollah's leadership or direct evidence of Syria; Syria and Hezbollah 'may have had motives'; Hezbollah denied involvement; fifth accused's case dropped after he was killed in Syria in 2016

Appeals chamber March 2022 convicted Merhi and Oneissi; 16 June 2022 sentenced to life in absentia; Ayyash sentenced to life in 2020; Hezbollah refused to surrender them and Nasrallah refused to recognise the court; court cost estimated $600m-$1bn, 51% donors 49% Lebanon

July 2011 STL indicted four Hezbollah members; Nasrallah: they could not be arrested 'in 30 days or 60 days, or in a year, two years, 30 years or 300 years'; Hezbollah and allies resigned from government in 2011 over the tribunal
Port blast 4 Aug 2020 killed about 220; Hezbollah reportedly tried to quash investigation; Nasrallah denied responsibility
Wafiq Safa reportedly told judicial superiors on 20 Sept 2021 'should he drift off the course, we will remove him'; reported by Lebanese media
Bitar described the warning in a letter to the prosecutor and justice minister; Safa did not respond; Bitar had not sought to question Hezbollah members, only allied politicians
Nasrallah 11 Oct 2021: Bitar using 'the blood of the victims to serve political interests'; 'clearly political targeting'; called on Higher Judicial Council

Tayouneh 14 Oct 2021: Amal/Hezbollah protest against Bitar's warrant for Ali Hassan Khalil; seven killed (three Amal, three Hezbollah, one woman), about 30 injured; Amal and Hezbollah blamed Lebanese Forces, LF denied; Nasrallah 18 Oct accused LF of seeking civil war; no official findings published by Oct 2022
Probe stalled after Hezbollah accused Bitar of bias and officials filed lawsuits; Oueidat blocked resumption early 2023; Bitar resumed 16 Jan 2025 and charged 10
Bitar submitted his report late March 2026, reportedly accusing 70 people; no indictment as of 4 August 2026

Oct 2019 attacks on protesters: Nabatieh 23 Oct 400+ men identified by protesters as Hezbollah supporters; Beirut 29 Oct attackers chanting for Berri and Nasrallah burned tents in Martyrs' Square; no arrests; at least six security-force failures
